BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r1.claim: After recalling earlier prophets and believers who endured harm and remained steadfast, the Prophet too should persist in monotheism and its call until God's command arrives.
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r1.anchor: أحوال القرون الأولى وأن إخوانك الأنبياء ومؤمنيهم تحملوا من قومهم الأذى

BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r2.claim: ‘Those who repented with you’ coordinates with the implicit subject of ‘be steadfast’; they are believers who turned from unbelief and share faith, not a claim that prophets repented from unbelief.
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r2.anchor: معطوف على المستكن في فاستقم من غير تأكيد

BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r3.claim: Prophets are unanimously protected from unbelief and deliberate major sins before and after revelation; shared repentance can mean turning together without sharing the same past sin.
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r3.anchor: معصومون عن الكفر وكذا عن تعمد الكبائر قبل الوحي وبعده بالإجماع

BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r4.claim: He suggests repentance here means leaving one's former state, whether it involved actual unbelief or not, as with the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r4.anchor: لعل التوبة في مثل هذا المقام هي الرجوع عن الحالة الأولى ومفارقتها

BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r5.claim: The Prophet testified that ʿAlī never disbelieved in God even for an instant; inviting him to reject al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā does not prove he had been an unbeliever.
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r5.anchor: شهد بأن عليا رضي الله عنه لم يكفر بالله قط طرفة عين

BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r6.claim: Do not transgress the set limits through excess or deficiency, since both extremes are blameworthy; ‘transgression’ emphasizes the warning or generalizes from most believers.
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r6.anchor: أي ولا تنحرفوا عما حد لكم بإفراط وتفريط

BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r7.claim: The prohibition parallels another sūra's command not to follow unbelievers' desires: avoiding them preserves full steadfastness, while following them is transgression.
BURSEVI:v4p123#2/r7.anchor: والنهيان متقاربان إذ المراد عدم الاتباع لإهواء أهل الكفر

QASHANI:11:112-113/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:112-113/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:112-113/r1.claim: Steadfastness means fulfilling God's rights through God: the Prophet upholds divine commands while witnessing unity after returning to creation, without egoic coloring or neglecting moral duties.
QASHANI:11:112-113/r1.anchor: في القيام بحقوق الله بالله، فإنه عليه الصلاة والسلام مأمور بمحافظة حقوق الله

QASHANI:11:112-113/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:112-113/r2.speaker: عليه السلام
QASHANI:11:112-113/r2.claim: The Prophet says that even with divine forgiveness he should remain a grateful servant, after his feet swelled from night worship.
QASHANI:11:112-113/r2.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أفلا أكون عبدا شكورا؟ " حين تورمت قدماه

QASHANI:11:112-113/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:112-113/r3.speaker: عليه السلام
QASHANI:11:112-113/r3.claim: A report recounts an ʿārif seeing the Prophet ask why Sūrat Hūd had made him gray; the Prophet says the cause is the command to remain steadfast, not the stories of punished peoples.
QASHANI:11:112-113/r3.anchor: رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعض العرفاء في المنام، فسأله عن ذلك

QASHANI:11:112-113#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:112-113#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:112-113#2/r1.claim: Those who repent with the Prophet abandon self-assertion and the sin of self-existence, realizing multiplicity within unity and subsistence after annihilation.
QASHANI:11:112-113#2/r1.anchor: من الموحدين الواصلين إلى شهود الكثرة في عين الوحدة

QASHANI:11:112-113#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:112-113#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:112-113#2/r2.claim: Do not overstep by assigning unqualified divine perfection to the delimited ego, which veils God's identity beyond individuation; God sees whether deeds are through Him or the self.
QASHANI:11:112-113#2/r2.anchor: نسبة الكمالات الإلهية المطلقة إلى أنائيتكم المشخصة المقيدة

QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r1.claim: Those who repent with the Prophet must also remain upright.

QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r2.claim: Uprightness includes refusing to imitate, praise, socialize with, or inwardly approve the unjust, while continuing to forbid wrongdoing and avoid unlawful wealth.
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r2.anchor: ولا ترضوا بأعمالهم ، ولا تمدحوهم على أعمالهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r3.claim: Every moment should be filled with worship; losing even one moment of an obligatory or voluntary act is a grave regret and loss.
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r3.anchor: إخلالك لحظة من الزمان بفرض تؤديه ، أو نفل تأتيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r1.speaker: ابن عيينة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna and a group interpret istiqama as remaining firm upon the Quran.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r1.anchor: قال ابن عيينة وجماعة: معناه استقم على القرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r2.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets istiqama as persevering in jihad.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r3.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r3.claim: Muqatil says istiqama means continuing upon monotheism.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r4.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r4.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq interprets istiqama as truthful reporting about God with firm resolve.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r4.anchor: وقال جعفر الصادق: استقم في الإخبار عن الله بصحة العزم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses the command as maintaining the commanded straightness on the path of truth without departing from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فاستقم استقامة مثل الاستقامة التي أمرت بها على جادة الحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the Prophet was already upright, so the command requires lasting constancy; it addresses him, his believing companions, and the whole community, with the plural form honoring the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: أمر بالاستقامة وهو عليها، وهو أمر بالدوام والثبوت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r7.claim: استفعل may here express seeking, so istiqama can mean asking to be established in religion; ومن تاب coordinates with the hidden subject after a separator makes explicit reinforcement unnecessary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r7.anchor: استفعل هنا للطلب أي: اطلب الإقامة على الدين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains not transgressing as refusing to declare lawful or unlawful anything God did not command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r8.anchor: ولا تطغوا قال ابن عباس: في القرآن فتحلوا وتحرموا ما لم آمركم به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says not to transgress means not to disobey the Lord; Muqatil says not to mix monotheism with doubt, and al-Zamakhshari says not to cross God's bounds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r9.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: لا تعصوا ربكم. وقال مقاتل: لا تخلطوا التوحيد بالشك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r10.speaker: الحسن، والأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r10.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Aʿmash read the final phrase with third-person plural verbs, and the reading is also attributed to ʿIsa al-Thaqafi; بصير means God sees their deeds and repays them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p220/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعمش: بما يعملون بالياء على الغيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r3.claim: Addressing the Prophet directly in commands to do good, while directing prohibitions to the community, is a mark of eloquence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r3.anchor: حيث كان بأفعال الخير توجه الخطاب إليه، وحيث كان النهي عن المحظورات

AKHFASH:v1p391/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p391/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p391/r1.claim: تطغوا comes from طغوت تطغا, like محوت تمحا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#4/r1.claim: Istaqim means continue along what you were commanded.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#4/r1.anchor: {فاستقم كما أمرت} أي: امض على ما أمرت به.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r1.claim: After explaining disputes over monotheism and prophethood and promises and threats, God commands the Messenger to remain steadfast as commanded, implying another revelation, perhaps non-recited.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r1.anchor: لما بين أمر المختلفين في التوحيد والنبوة وأطنب سبحانه في شرح الوعد والوعيد أمر رسوله

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r2.claim: Uprightness is lasting adherence to the balanced path between excess and deficiency, comprehensive of knowledge, action, character, beliefs, shared duties, and the Prophet’s special mission.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا أمر بالدوام على الإستقامة وهي لزوم المنهج المستقيم وهو المتوسط بين الإفراط والتفريط

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r3.claim: Perfect balance requires total dependence on God; it is likened to a line between sun and shade, and its difficulty is illustrated by 17:74. It requires spiritual support and clinging to truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r3.anchor: لا يحصل إلا بالإفتقار إلى الله تعالى ونفي الحول والقوة بالكلية ومثلوا الأمر المتوسط بين ذينك الطرفين بخط يكون بين الشمس والظل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r4.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that after this verse descended, the Prophet said ‘Be earnest, be earnest,’ and was not seen laughing afterward; Ibn ʿAbbās called it the hardest verse to bear.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r4.anchor: عن الحسن أنه قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية قال صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : شمروا شمروا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r5.claim: Some cite ‘Hūd made me gray’ as proof of hardship, but reports add other sūrahs too; al-Kashf says singling out Hūd is not evident because its sister sūrahs do not mention uprightness.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r5.anchor: من قوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : شيبتني هود

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r6.speaker: ابن عساكر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAsākir transmits from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, the Prophet’s statement that Hūd, its sister sūrahs, and what befell earlier nations made him gray.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152/r6.anchor: ما أخرجه ابن عساكر عن جعفر بن محمد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r1.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r1.claim: Al-Shihāb explains Hūd’s special effect by its structure: it guides the Prophet through the methods and hardships of calling people from beginning to end, rather than merely consoling him.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r1.anchor: مبنى هذه السورة الكريمة على إرشاده تعالى شأنه نبيه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إلى كيفية الدعوة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r2.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r2.claim: This concluding verse summarizes the sūrah; its burdens made the Prophet fear accountability for failing them. Other sūrahs’ Judgment scenes recalled Hūd’s guidance, without implying any conflict with infallibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r2.anchor: ولما كانت هذه السورة جامعة لإرشاده من أول أمره إلى آخرخ وهذه الآية فذلكة لها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r3.claim: The report continues that Hūd and its sister sūrahs and what earlier nations suffered made the Prophet gray; this does not conflict with reports naming Hūd alone or this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r3.anchor: قال : شيبتني هود وأخواتها وما فعل بالأمم قبلي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others take kāf in kamā as ‘upon,’ meaning remain upon the Qurʾān; Muqātil says remain upon monotheism, and Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says report truthfully about God with firm resolve.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطية وجماعة : المعنى إستقم على القرآن وقال مقاتل : إمض على التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the broad sense: remain upright in everything God commanded.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r5.anchor: والأظهر إبقاء ما على العموم أي إستقم على جميع ما أمرت به

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r6.claim: Another account keeps kāf comparative but treats it like mathal in ‘one like you is not miserly’; al-Ālūsī says comparing a thing with itself is unnecessary. Abū Ḥayyān supplies ‘the like of what the command seeks.’
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r6.anchor: إنها في حكم مثل في قولهم : مثلك لا يبخل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r7.claim: A more remote reading makes kāf mean ‘upon’ and istifʿāl a request, yielding ‘seek establishment upon the religion.’
ALUSI-FULL:v12p152#2/r7.anchor: وأبعد بعضهم فجعل الكاف بمعنى على واستفعل للطلب كاستغفر الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r1.claim: Those who repented with the Prophet abandoned associating partners and believed with him; their companionship may refer to shared repentance without specifying its object.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r1.anchor: ومن تاب معك ( أي تاب من الشرك وآمن معك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r2.claim: The Prophet used to seek God’s forgiveness more than seventy times daily.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r2.anchor: يستغفر الله تعالى في اليوم أكثر من سبعين مرة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān and others coordinate man with the implicit subject of ‘be steadfast’; others prefer an omitted verb because an imperative does not take an overt subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r3.anchor: و ( من ) على ما اختاره أبو حيان وجماعة عطف على الضمير المستكن في ( واستقم )

ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows a comitative object: be steadfast alongside those who repented; a nominal clause with an omitted predicate is another view.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r4.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء كونه منصوبا على أنه مفعول معه والمعنى استقم مصاحبا لمن تاب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r5.claim: Do not exceed bounds by excess or deficiency; Ibn ʿAbbās says not to declare Qurʾānic lawful and unlawful without command, Ibn Zayd says do not disobey God, and Muqātil says do not mix monotheism with idolatry; the broad sense is preferred.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r5.anchor: ولا تطغوا ( أي لا تنحرفوا عما حد لكم بإفراط أو تفريط فإن كلا طرفي قصد الأمور ذميم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r6.claim: God sees and recompenses people’s acts; this explains the preceding command and prohibition. Some read the verb in the third person.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r6.anchor: فيجازيكم على ذلك وهو تعليل للأمر والنهي السابقين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r7.claim: Some infer that explicit texts must be followed without bending them to desire or unaided reason; analogy grounded in textual causes counts as following authorized ijtihād. The Imam objects to specifying general texts by analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p153/r7.anchor: دليل على وجوب إتباع المنصوص عليه من غير إنحراف بمجرد التشهي وإعمال العقل الصرف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p154/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p154/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p154/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the Imam’s proof that ablution limbs must follow Qurʾānic word order: the same logic would order every pair of commands joined by wa, such as prayer and alms, which is untenable.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p154/r1.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن إيجاب الترتيب في الوضوء لذلك ليس بشيء ويلزمه أن يوجب الترتيب في الأوامر المتعاطفة بالواو

ALUSI-FULL:v12p154/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p154/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p154/r2.claim: The argument unjustly implies that Ḥanafīs who do not require ablution order are tyrants outside God’s bounds, with no possibility of being upright.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p154/r2.anchor: يجزم بأن الحنفية الذين لا يوجبون الترتيب في أعمال الوضوء طاغون خارجون عما حد الله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r1.claim: Steadfastness means remaining on the Lord’s religion, practicing it, and calling others to it; those who believe with Muhammad must also remain steadfast.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r1.anchor: أي: استقم على دين ربك، والعمل به، والدعاء إليه كما أمرت، {ومن تاب معك} أي: ومن آمن معك فليستقيموا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r2.claim: Umar defines steadfastness as keeping to commands and prohibitions without twisting away like a fox.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r2.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: الاستقامة أن تستقيم على الأمر والنهي، ولا تروغ روغان الثعلب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r3.speaker: سفيان بن عبد الله الثقفي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r3.claim: Sufyan ibn Abd Allah asked the Prophet for a concise instruction; he replied, “Say I believe in God, then be steadfast.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203/r3.anchor: عن سفيان بن عبد الله الثقفي قال: قلت، يا رسول الله قل لي في الإسلام قولا لا أسأل عنه أحدا بعدك،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r1.claim: Do not transgress means neither disobey God’s command nor exceed what He commanded and forbade.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r1.anchor: لا تجاوزوا أمري ولا تعصوني، وقيل: معناه ولا تغلوا فتزيدوا على ما أمرت ونهيت.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r2.claim: God sees all their actions and nothing is hidden from Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r2.anchor: {إنه بما تعملون بصير} لا يخفى عليه من أعمالكم شيء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says no verse weighed more heavily on the Prophet; he said Hud and its sister chapters had made him gray.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: ما نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم آية هي أشد عليه من هذه الآية،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s teaching that religion is easy; do not overburden yourselves, but act moderately, rejoice, and seek help at different times of day and night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p203#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الدين يسر ولن يشاد الدين أحد إلا غلبه،

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r1.claim: The command follows the account of disagreement over unity and prophecy and the detailed promise and threat; steadfastness covers balanced belief between anthropomorphism and negation, faithful transmission of revelation and law, and proper worship without excess or neglect.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r1.anchor: وهي شاملة للاستقامة في العقائد كالتوسط بين التشبيه والتعطيل

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r2.claim: The Prophet said that Hud made him gray-haired, alluding to the difficulty of steadfastness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r2.anchor:
ولذلك قال عليه الصلاة والسلام
" شيبتني هود "

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r3.claim: Those who repented with Muhammad are people who left idolatry and disbelief and believed; the phrase coordinates them with the implied subject of 'be steadfast.'
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r3.anchor: { ومن تاب معك } أي تاب من الشرك والكفر وآمن معك، وهو عطف

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r4.claim: Do not go beyond the limits set for you; God sees deeds and will recompense them, which explains both the command and prohibition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r4.anchor: { ولا تطغوا } ولا تخرجوا عما حد لكم. { إنه بما تعملون بصير } فهو مجازيكم عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r5.claim: The verse requires following revealed texts without altering or deviating from them through analogy or juristic preference.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:112/r5.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على وجوب اتباع النصوص من غير تصرف وانحراف بنحو قياس واستحسان

BIQAI-FULL:v3p583/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p583/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p583/r6.claim: The Prophet must exert himself to stand firm as commanded, in personal conduct and conveying the message, following earlier prophets in roots and branches, without being unsettled by mockery or demands to conceal revelation.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p583/r6.anchor: بغاية جهدك بسبب أنك لا تلكف إلا نفسك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r1.claim: Those who repented from disbelief must also remain upright with the Prophet and not become anxious about delayed help.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r1.anchor: ولما كان الفاصل بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليه يقوم مقام تأكيد الضمير المستتر

BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r2.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r2.claim: Khabbab reports that the Prophet recalled believers tortured by sawing and iron combs who stayed faithful, then promised Islam's completion and safe travel from Sana'a to Hadramawt; he told his impatient hearers they were hasty.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r2.anchor: كما روى البخاري وابو داود والنسائي عن خباب بن الأرت رضي الله عنه قال : شكونا إلى رسول الله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says no verse was harder or more burdensome for the Prophet than this one.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ما نزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آية اشد ولا أشق من هذه الآية

BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r4.claim: Uprightness means continuing along one course; the command is moderate between excess and neglect, and people rarely escape neglect, which can humble them, while excess breeds pride and can make someone act as a lawgiver.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r5.claim: Do not exceed the limits of commands or prohibitions: religion is moderate, intended to discipline people rather than meet God's need, and modest practice with sound purpose is sufficient.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r5.anchor: { ولا تطغوا } أي تتجاوزوا الحد فيما أمرتم به أو نهيتم عنه بالزيادة إفراطا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r6.claim: The prohibition of excess also implies, a fortiori, a prohibition of falling short; alternatively, it warns against letting prosperity make one arrogant or deviate from the straight path.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r6.anchor: ولما نهى عن الإفراط وهو الزيادة تصريحا , فأفهم النهي عن التفريط

BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r7.claim: The root of طغى revolves around exceeding a limit while rising; the author connects its derivatives to covering, night, flood, sea, disobedience, fertile lowlands, and Syria's well-watered Ghuta.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p584/r7.anchor: ومادة ( طغى ) واوية ويائية بكل ترتيب تدور على مجاوزة الحد مع العلو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r1.claim: After consolation and reassurance, the Prophet is urged to persist in Islam's straight path and remain constant in its teachings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r1.anchor: وعبر عن ذلك بالاستقامة لإفادة الدوام على العمل بتعاليم الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r2.claim: Believers are included because deviation from scripture invites factions to alter it; upright practice of the complete law after faith prevents such disagreement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r2.anchor: لأن الاعوجاج من دواعي الاختلاف في الكتاب بنهوض فرق من الأمة إلى تبديله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r3.claim: A hadith says earlier peoples were destroyed by excessive questioning and disagreement with their prophets; uprightness means carrying out the law without deviation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r3.anchor: فإنما أهلك الذين من قبلكم كثرة مسائلهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r4.claim: The Prophet's direct address honors him as the first recipient; “as you were commanded” makes his straightness the model for the community.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r5.claim: The comparison in “as commanded” is a circumstantial phrase equating uprightness with all other commands, effectively meaning “remain as you are.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p175/r5.anchor: يؤول هذا المعنى إلى أن تكون الكاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r1.claim: “Those who repent with you” coordinates with the attached pronoun in “you were commanded”; the intervening prepositional phrase licenses the coordination.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r1.anchor: ومصحح العطف موجود وهو الفصل بالجار والمجرور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r2.claim: “Those who repent” are believers, since faith is repentance from associating partners; “with you” is circumstantial, not an attachment to repent.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r3.claim: The command to be upright gathers the foundations and branches of religious rectitude.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says no verse was harder for the Prophet; when companions noticed his gray hair, he said Hud and its sisters had made him gray, and when asked what in Hud he cited this command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r4.anchor: ابن عباس : ما نزل على رسول الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r5.claim: “Do not transgress” addresses the believers included in “those with you.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r5.anchor: موجه إلى المؤمنين الذين صدق عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r6.claim: Transgression originally means arrogance and audacity; here it means daring to violate commands, as in the warning to Israel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r6.anchor: والمراد هنا الجراءة على مخالفة ما أمروا به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r9.claim: God's seeing warns against concealed transgression; “seeing” was chosen to convey clear and powerful knowledge of every deed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p176/r9.anchor: من بين بقية الأسماء الحسنى لدلالة مادته على العلم البين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r1.claim: Although the Prophet is already upright, the command means to continue and remain steadfast, like telling someone already walking or eating to keep doing so; the address includes him and the Companions who repented from disbelief, and by implication the whole community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r1.anchor: أمر النبي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالاستقامة وهو عليها إنما هو أمر بالدوام والثبوت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r2.claim: A scholar reportedly saw the Prophet in a dream and asked what in Hud made him say it and its companion suras had made him gray; the Prophet answered, 'Be steadfast as you were commanded.' Ibn Atiyya says the well-known explanation is his fear that earlier peoples' fates might befall this community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r2.anchor: رأي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في النوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r3.claim: أمرت is an honorific plural form of address; ومن is coordinated with the pronoun in فاستقم, permitted without repeating it because كما أمرت makes the phrase long.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r3.anchor: ومن معطوف على الضمير في قوله: فاستقم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r4.claim: ولا تطغوا means do not exceed God's limits; طغيان is crossing the limit, as with the flood and Pharaoh, or specifically letting blessings lead to transgression.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r4.anchor: معناه: ولا تتجاوزوا حدود الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r5.claim: The majority read تعملون with second-person tāʾ; Hasan and al-A'mash read يعملون with third-person yāʾ, and readers vary between open and rounded kaf in تركنوا, with the latter a dialect form meaning to settle or be content with something.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p211#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «تعملون» بتاء، وقرأ الحسن والأعمش «يعملون»

SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r1.claim: كما أمرت is accusative as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun or as a circumstantial phrase from that noun's pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r1.anchor: الكاف في محل النصب: إما على النعت لمصدر محذوف، كما هو المشهور عند المعربين.

SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses the command as uprightness like that commanded, remaining on the path of truth without deviation; استقم is a request to maintain uprightness.
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " أي: استقم استقامة مثل الاستقامة التي أمرت بها على جادة الحق غير عادل عنها "

SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa parses ومن تاب معك as a comitative object, though the author says the resulting meaning is awkward.
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r3.anchor: قوله: { ومن تاب معك } في " من " وجهان

SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r4.claim: ومن تاب معك is nominative, coordinated with the hidden subject of استقم; the author follows the clause-level parse and Zamakhshari's sense, you be upright and let your followers be upright.
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r4.anchor: فإنه نسق على المستتر في " استقم "

SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r5.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r5.claim: The general reading uses the second-person ت in بما تعملون بصير, matching the preceding address.
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r5.anchor: وقرأ العامة { بما تعملون بصير } بالتاء جريا على الخطاب المتقدم.

SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r6.speaker: الحسن والأعمش وعيسى الثقفي
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r6.claim: They read بما يعملون with yāʾ, shifting from direct address to third-person reference as in 11:111.
SAMIN-DURR:11:112/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعمش وعيسى الثقفي بالياء للغيبة، وهو التفات من خطاب لغيبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354/r1.claim: God commands the Messenger and believers to persist in the prescribed straight path; steadfastness is a major aid to victory over enemies and opponents.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354/r1.anchor: يأمر تعالى رسوله وعباده المؤمنين بالثبات والدوام على الاستقامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354/r2.claim: They must not transgress: oppression is ruinous even when directed against polytheists, and God sees every deed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354/r2.anchor: ونهى عن الطغيان، وهو البغي، فإنه مصرعة حتى ولو كان على مشرك

JISHUMI:v5p3576/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r1.claim: The common reading of زلفا has ḍamma on zāy and fatḥa on lām; Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Mujāhid have other vocalizations, all dialect variants.
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: زلفا بضم الزاي، وفتح اللام، وقرأ أبو جعفر بضم الزاي واللام

JISHUMI:v5p3576/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r2.claim: Istiqāma is continuing along one direction; the word derives from q-w-m and belongs with forms such as aqāma and istaqāma.
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r2.anchor: الاستقامة: الاستمرار في جهة واحدة، وهو استفعال من قام يقوم، وأصله الواو

JISHUMI:v5p3576/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r3.claim: Ṭughyān is exceeding limits in disobedience or corruption; water and floods are described this way by analogy, and the root has variant forms.
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r3.anchor: الطغيان: تجاوز الحد في العصيان والفساد، فالطاغي اسم ذم كالباغي

JISHUMI:v5p3576/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r7.claim: The tāʾ in أمرت is a passive subject in the nominative, and ومن تاب coordinates with it; زلفا is accusative as an adverb of time.
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r7.anchor: التاء من (أمرت) في محل الرفع؛ لأنه فعل ما لم يسم فاعله

JISHUMI:v5p3576/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says no verse was harder on the Prophet than the command to remain upright, and that Sūrat Hūd and its sisters made him old.
JISHUMI:v5p3576/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس: ما نزلت آية كانت أشق على رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

JISHUMI:v5p3579/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r9.claim: Uprightness in religion is obligatory and consists of performing obligations and avoiding prohibitions; repentance for past sins is valid only with commitment to future duties.
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r9.anchor: تدل الآية على وجوب الاستقامة في الدين، والاستقامة أداء الواجبات، واجتناب المحرمات

MUQATIL:11:110-112/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:110-112/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:110-112/r3.claim: Muhammad and those who repented from shirk must persevere in monotheism without disobeying God in it.
MUQATIL:11:110-112/r3.anchor: { فاستقم } ، يعني فامض يا محمد بالتوحيد { كمآ أمرت ومن تاب معك } من الشرك، فليستقيموا معك،

NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r1.claim: The Prophet must remain on the commanded path without deviating; those who repent from disbelief and return sincerely to God are conjoined with him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r1.anchor: فاستقم استقامة مثل الاستقامة التى أمرت بها غير عادل عنها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r2.claim: The conjunction with the hidden subject is allowed because of the intervening phrase; believers must not cross God's limits, since God sees and recompenses their deeds.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r2.anchor: معطوف على المستتر فى استقم وجاز للفاصل يعنى فاستقم أنت

NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r3.claim: It is said that no verse was harder for the Prophet than this one, prompting the saying 'Hud has made me gray.'
NASAFI-FULL:v2p174/r3.anchor: قيل ما نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم آية كان اشق عليه من هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r1.claim: The command to be steadfast addresses the Prophet and others as well.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فاستقم كمآ أمرت } الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r2.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the command addresses the Prophet while intending his community.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r3.claim: Another explanation makes the command a request that God grant steadfastness; the prefix in استقم is like asking God for forgiveness, and steadfastness means staying on one course without deviation.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r3.anchor: استقم» اطلب الإقامة على الدين من الله واسأله ذلك. فتكون السين سين السؤال

QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r4.claim: In Muslim, Sufyan ibn Abdullah asks for a concise statement of Islam; the Prophet answers: believe in God, then remain steadfast.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r4.anchor: قال: قلت يا رسول الله قل لي في الإسلام قولا لا أسأل عنه أحدا بعدك

QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r5.claim: When Uthman ibn Hadir asked Ibn Abbas for advice, Ibn Abbas urged God-consciousness, steadfastness, following precedent, and avoiding innovation.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r5.anchor: وروى الدارمي أبو محمد في مسنده عن عثمان بن حاضر الأزدي قال: دخلت على ابن

QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r6.claim: Those who repented with the Prophet are his companions who left polytheism and later followers of his community; they too must remain steadfast.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r6.anchor: ومن تاب معك } أي استقم أنت وهم يريد أصحابه الذين تابوا من الشرك ومن بعده

QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says no verse was harder or more burdensome for the Prophet than this one.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r7.anchor: آية هي أشد ولا أشق من هذه الآية عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r8.claim: When companions noticed his rapid graying, the Prophet said Hud and its sister surahs had made him gray.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r8.anchor:
حين قالوا له: لقد أسرع إليك الشيب! فقال:
" شيبتني هود وأخواتها

QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r9.speaker: أبو علي السري
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r9.claim: In a dream recounted by Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, the Prophet said steadfastness in 11:112, rather than the prophets' stories or peoples' destruction, was what made him gray.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112/r9.anchor:
وروي
" عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال سمعت أبا علي السري يقول: رأيت النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:11:112#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112#2/r1.claim: Tughyan means exceeding the limit; the prohibition therefore bars transgression.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112#2/r1.anchor: ولا تطغوا } نهي عن الطغيان والطغيان مجاوزة الحد ومنه { إنا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:112#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112#2/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112#2/r2.claim: An alternative takes the prohibition as a ban on acting arrogantly or oppressively toward anyone.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:112#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: أي لا تتجبروا على أحد

RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r1.claim: After the preceding promise and threat, steadfastness is a comprehensive command for creed, practice, and preaching the revelation and laws.
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r1.anchor: اعلم أنه تعلى لما أطنب في شرح الوعد والوعيد قال لرسوله : { فاستقم كما أمرت }

RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r2.claim: True steadfastness is hard to discern, like the single boundary between shadow and light that the eye cannot distinguish from either side.
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r2.anchor: الخط المستقيم الذي يفصل بين الظل وبين الضوء جزء واحد لا يقبل القسمة

RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r3.claim: The servant must avoid both anthropomorphism and negation in knowing God and find a difficult middle course between excess and deficiency in anger and desire; remaining on that path is harder still.
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r3.anchor: مصونا في طرف الإثبات عن التشبيه ، وفي طرف النفي عن التعطيل في غاية الصعوبة

RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says no Qurʾānic verse was harder for the Prophet than this one.
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ما نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جميع القرآن آية أشد

RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r5.claim: A prophetic report says Sūrat Hūd and its sisters made the Prophet's hair gray; a dream narrative identifies this steadfastness verse as the cause.
RAZI-FULL:v18p56#3/r5.anchor: شيبتني هود وأخواتها ، وعن بعضهم قال : رأيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في النوم

RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r1.claim: The command to be steadfast is a foundational legal principle: follow the stated order in ablution and give like livestock in zakāt, as in all divine commands.
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r1.anchor: هذه الآية أصل عظيم في الشريعة وذلك لأن القرآن لما ورد بالأمر بأعمال الوضوء

RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r2.claim: Rāzī rejects qualifying a general text by analogy because its clear command must be followed and analogy departs from it.
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r2.anchor: وعندي أنه لا يجوز تخصيص النص بالقياس ، لأنه لما دل عموم النص على حكم

RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r3.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r3.claim: Al-Wāḥidī gives three parses for ومن تاب: coordination with the implied subject of be steadfast, with the subject of “I commanded,” or a new clause meaning the repentant should be steadfast.
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r3.anchor: قال الواحدي : من في محل الرفع من وجوه : الأول : أن يكون عطفا على الضمير المستتر

RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r4.claim: A person still in unbelief or sin cannot yet follow the straight path; after repentance, the person can practice the religion and remain in God's service.
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r4.anchor: وأما التائب عن الكفر والفسق فإنه يصح منه الاشتغال بالاستقامة

RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets “do not transgress” as humility toward God and not acting arrogantly toward anyone.
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد تواضعوا لله تعالى ولا تتكبروا على أحد

RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r6.claim: Other interpretations prohibit distorting the Qurʾān's lawful and unlawful rules, exceeding God's limits, or abandoning gratitude and humility; the author prefers that the phrase include all of them.
RAZI-FULL:v18p57/r6.anchor: والأولى دخول الكل فيه ، ثم قال : { ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا }

ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r1.speaker: Ibn Kathir
ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir takes the plural injunction as addressed to all believers and governing their conduct toward everyone, believer or unbeliever, following Ibn Abbas.
ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r1.anchor: Ibn Kathir points out that it is addressed to all believers, and that it refers to their behaviour towards everyone

ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r2.speaker: Ibn 'Abbas
ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the injunction as humility before God and avoiding false pride toward anyone.
ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r2.anchor: Be humble before God and do not behave with false pride towards anyone

ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r3.speaker: Tabari, Zamakhshari, Baghawi, Razi
ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r3.claim: Later commentators broaden the command to mean staying within God's limits and not exceeding equity.
ASAD-NOTES:11:111#n141/r3.anchor: or "do not exceed the limits of equity"

STUDYQURAN:11:112/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:112/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:112/r1.claim: The command to remain steadfast is addressed to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:11:112/r1.anchor: Be steadfast, a command addressed to the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:11:112/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:112/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:11:112/r2.claim: Some interpret steadfastness as holding firmly to the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:11:112/r2.anchor: understood by some to mean that he should hold steadfastly to the Quran (R)

STUDYQURAN:11:112/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:112/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:11:112/r3.claim: The command extends to those who repent alongside the Prophet, identified here as his Companions.
STUDYQURAN:11:112/r3.anchor: it is a command also directed toward those who turn in repentance along with him, namely, the Prophet’s Companions (Q)

TAB-FULL:v12p598/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r1.claim: Muhammad must remain steadfast in the religion and call to it as God commanded, and those who returned with him must obey God after disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r1.anchor: طاعة الله، والعمل بما أمره به ربه من بعد كفره

TAB-FULL:v12p598/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r2.claim: Do not transgress God's command by doing what He forbade; God sees and knows every act of obedience or disobedience, and nothing is hidden from Him.
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r2.anchor: طاعة الله، والعمل بما أمره به ربه من بعد كفره

TAB-FULL:v12p598/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r3.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r3.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna interprets steadfastness as remaining upon the Qur'an.
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r3.anchor: في قوله: " {فاستقم كما أمرت} [هود: 112] قال: استقم على القرآن

TAB-FULL:v12p598/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd defines transgression as opposing God and committing disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v12p598/r4.anchor: في قوله: " {ولا تطغوا} [هود: 112] قال: الطغيان: خلاف الله وركوب معصيته

TABATABAI:11:112/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:112/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:112/r1.claim: Standing signifies a person's stable, empowered state; the image extends to anything established so that it can produce its full effects, including justice, law, prayer, testimony, and religion.
TABATABAI:11:112/r1.anchor: ثم استعير في كل شيء لأعدل حالاته الذي يسلط معه على آثاره وأعماله

TABATABAI:11:112/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:112/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:112/r2.claim: Iqama sets something upright so all intended effects remain available; istiqama seeks and sustains that complete functioning, as with a straight road or a person perfecting an undertaking.
TABATABAI:11:112/r2.anchor: والاستقامة طلب القيام من الشيء واستدعاء ظهور عامة آثاره ومنافعه

TABATABAI:11:112/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:112/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:112/r3.claim: The command means steadfastly fulfilling religion and its right, maintaining monotheism in inward and outward life, as explained by earlier commands to face religion sincerely.
TABATABAI:11:112/r3.anchor: أي كن ثابتا على الدين موفيا حقه طبق ما أمرت

TABATABAI:11:112/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:112/r4.speaker: صاحب روح المعاني
TABATABAI:11:112/r4.claim: Alusi suggests as commanded may refer to another, unrecited revelation and calls istiqama a comprehensive middle path between excess and neglect.
TABATABAI:11:112/r4.anchor: قال في روح المعاني أمر رسوله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالاستقامه مثل الاستقامة التي أمر بها

TABATABAI:11:112/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:112/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:112/r5.claim: He rejects an appeal to an unmentioned revelation: the Qur'an had already commanded the Prophet to establish himself upon religion, so no hidden instruction is needed.
TABATABAI:11:112/r5.anchor: أما احتماله أن يكون هناك وحي آخر غير متلو يشير إليه قوله

TABATABAI:11:112#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r1.claim: Istiqama here is full and steady performance of servitude, not merely moderation between extremes; the following ban on transgression targets excess and clarifies the command.
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r1.anchor: ولو كان المراد بالأمر بالاستقامة هو الامر بلزوم الاعتدال بين الإفراط والتفريط

TABATABAI:11:112#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r2.claim: Transgression means crossing the limits of human servitude through pride and refusal to submit, as earlier peoples did; the verb evokes water exceeding its bounds.
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r2.anchor: ثم نهى عن تعدي هذا الطور والاستكبار عن الخضوع لله

TABATABAI:11:112#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r3.claim: And those who repent coordinates with the hidden subject of stand firm: believers who returned from shirk through faith; the Prophet is singled out to honor his office.
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r3.anchor: أي استقم أنت ومن تاب معك أي استقيموا جميعا

TABATABAI:11:112#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r4.claim: As you were commanded applies specifically to the Prophet, because the earlier command to establish religion's direction addressed him alone.
TABATABAI:11:112#2/r4.anchor: يختص بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ولا يشاركه فيه غيره

TABATABAI:11:112-113/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:112-113/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:112-113/r1.claim: The verse commands steadfastness in monotheism and servitude, requires believers to stand firm, and warns them not to cross God's limits because He sees their deeds.
TABATABAI:11:112-113/r1.anchor: أثبت على دين التوحيد وألزم طريق العبودية من غير تزلزل وتذبذب

TABATABAI:11:112-113/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:112-113/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:112-113/r2.claim: The severe address singles out the Prophet and follows accounts of earlier nations' destruction, intensifying the warning.
TABATABAI:11:112-113/r2.anchor: وفي الآية الكريمة من لحن التشديد ما لا يخفى

TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r6.speaker: الحسن
TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r6.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmit from Hasan that when the command to stand firm was revealed, the believers girded themselves and the Prophet was no longer seen laughing.
TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r6.anchor: عن الحسن قال لما نزلت هذه الآية

TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says no verse was harder on the Prophet than the command to stand firm; the report explains his saying that Hud and al-Waqi'a made his hair gray.
TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس ما نزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم آية كانت أشد عليه ولا أشق

TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r8.claim: The familiar wording is Hud and its sisters; because al-Waqi'a lacks a parallel command, the author thinks the shared reference may instead be the Resurrection.
TABATABAI:11:109-119#3/r8.anchor: وعدم اشتمال الواقعة على ما يناظر قوله

TABRISI:11:109-112/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:109-112/r1.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:11:109-112/r1.claim: Abu Ali discusses a transmitted reading with tanwin on لما and compares it with the phrase أكلا لما, where the verbal noun describes the action.
TABRISI:11:109-112/r1.anchor: وقد روي أنه قد قرأ وإن كلا لما منونا كما قال وتأكلون التراث أكلا لما

TABRISI:11:109-112/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:109-112/r2.speaker: الكسائي
TABRISI:11:109-112/r2.claim: Al-Kisa'i says he does not know why لما is doubled; Abu Ali accepts that this difficulty is real.
TABRISI:11:109-112/r2.anchor: وقد حكي عن الكسائي أنه قال لا أعرف وجه التثقيل في لما ولم يبعد فيما قال

TABRISI:11:109-112/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:109-112/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:11:109-112/r3.claim: Abu Ali says the doubled form could mean ما كل إلا ليوفينهم if إن were light and كل nominative, parallel to the cited expression; then لما could more readily be an adjective of indefinite كل.
TABRISI:11:109-112/r3.anchor: على أن يكون المعنى ما كل إلا ليوفينهم فيكون ذلك كقوله وإن كل ذلك لما متاع الحياة الدنيا

TABRISI:11:109-112/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:109-112/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:109-112/r4.claim: The syntactic analysis would require كل to be annexed to an indefinite noun so لما can modify it; a definite annexation would block that adjective reading, and no clause element governs it as a circumstantial phrase.
TABRISI:11:109-112/r4.anchor: وينبغي أن يقدر المضاف إليه كل نكرة ليحسن وصفه بالنكرة

TABRISI:11:109-112/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:109-112/r5.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:11:109-112/r5.claim: Al-Farra' takes لما as لمن ما, with one of the three mims deleted, and cites a poetic line.
TABRISI:11:109-112/r5.anchor: قول الفراء: أنها بمعنى لمن ما فحذفت إحدى الميمات الثلاث

TABRISI:11:109-112/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:109-112/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:11:109-112/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes لما as إلا, but al-Farra' says that use is restricted to oaths, as Abu Ali argues.
TABRISI:11:109-112/r6.anchor: أنها بمعنى إلا كقولهم سألتك لما فعلت بمعنى إلا فعلت عن الزجاج

TABRISI:11:109-112/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:109-112/r7.speaker: المازني
TABRISI:11:109-112/r7.claim: Al-Mazini says لما is a lightened form that was doubled for emphasis; al-Zajjaj rejects this because Arabic permits weakening a doubled form only under poetic necessity, not doubling a light form.
TABRISI:11:109-112/r7.anchor: أنها مخففة شددت للتأكيد عن المازني قال الزجاج: هذا لا يجوز

TABRISI:11:109-112/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:109-112/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:109-112/r8.claim: A fourth proposal derives لما from gathering, builds it on فعلى without declension like تترى, and reads it as all together; al-Zuhri's tanwin reading supports this.
TABRISI:11:109-112/r8.anchor: أنها من لممت الشيء إذا جمعته إلا أنها بنيت على فعلى فلم تصرف

TABRISI:11:109-112/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:109-112/r9.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:11:109-112/r9.claim: Ibn Jinni parses لما as a comprehensive fulfillment of all their deeds, like using قياما for emphatic emphasis.
TABRISI:11:109-112/r9.anchor: وقال ابن جني تقديره هذا وإن كلا ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم لما أي توفية جامعة

TABRISI:11:109-112/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:109-112/r10.speaker: علي ابن أبي الطيب
TABRISI:11:109-112/r10.claim: Ali ibn Abi al-Tayyib supplies a fifth analysis with an omitted phrase, وإن كلا لما عملوا ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم, as the poem illustrates ellipsis.
TABRISI:11:109-112/r10.anchor: وذكر الشيخ علي ابن أبي الطيب رحمة الله عليه فيه وجها آخر فقال ها هنا محذوف

TABRISI:11:112/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:112/r1.claim: Mirya means doubt despite clear evidence; a share is an allotted portion; disagreement can be incompatible opposites or different valid judgments such as facing the qibla; istiqama is staying straight, and transgression exceeds the proper measure in corruption.
TABRISI:11:112/r1.anchor: المرية بكسر الميم وضمها الشك مع ظهور الدلالة للتهمة

TABRISI:11:112/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:112/r8.claim: When إن is light and كل is accusative after a negative sense, the analysis remains difficult; proposals inserting وإن هم إلا or an explanatory كلا are disfavored.
TABRISI:11:112/r8.anchor: فانتصاب كلا مع حمل أن على النفي مشكل

TABRISI:11:112/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:112/r9.claim: The reading وإن كل إلا ليوفينهم can mean God will certainly repay each one, with إلا treated as an extra particle if إن is lightened.
TABRISI:11:112/r9.anchor: ومن قرأ وإن كل إلا ليوفينهم فمعناه

TABRISI:11:112/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:112/r10.claim: For the experts, doubling the m of لما alongside either doubled or light إن remains problematic: it yields none of the known senses of لم, حين, or إلا.
TABRISI:11:112/r10.anchor: فإن تشديد الميم من لما مع تشديد إن وتخفيفه مشكل عند المحققين

TABRISI:11:112/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:112/r11.claim: The related poem uses إلا as an extra particle, meaning the era makes its people confused and leaves petitioners frustrated.

TABRISI:11:112#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:112#2/r1.claim: Muhammad is commanded to remain steadfast in preaching and warning, holding to obedience and calling people to practice it as the Qur'an commands; steadfastness means doing what is commanded and avoiding what is prohibited.
TABRISI:11:112#2/r1.anchor: استقم على الوعظ والإنذار والتمسك بالطاعة والأمر بها والدعاء عليها

TABRISI:11:112#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:11:112#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas takes those who repented with Muhammad as people who repented from associating partners with God and must also remain steadfast.
TABRISI:11:112#2/r2.anchor: وليستقم من تاب معك من الشرك كما أمروا عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:11:112#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:112#2/r3.claim: Another view applies it to all believers who turn back to God and His Prophet; a further parsing has Muhammad maintain delivery while they maintain acceptance.
TABRISI:11:112#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه ومن رجع إلى الله وإلى نبيه فليستقم أيضا

TABRISI:11:112#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:112#2/r4.claim: They are forbidden to exceed God's command through additions or omissions, which would take them outside steadfastness.
TABRISI:11:112#2/r4.anchor: لا تجاوزوا أمر الله بالزيادة والنقصان فتخرجوا عن حد الاستقامة

TABRISI:11:112#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112#2/r5.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:11:112#2/r5.claim: Al-Jubba'i warns that worldly blessing could make them transgress and leave the bounds of steadfastness.
TABRISI:11:112#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه ولا تطغينكم النعمة فتخرجوا عن حد الاستقامة عن الجبائي

TABRISI:11:112#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:112#2/r6.claim: Another gloss says simply not to disobey or oppose God; He sees all their actions and nothing is hidden from Him.
TABRISI:11:112#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا تعصوا الله ولا تخالفوه

TABRISI:11:112#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله
TABRISI:11:112#2/r7.claim: A report from Umar says even extreme prayer and fasting would not attain steadfastness if people preferred two over one.
TABRISI:11:112#2/r7.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

TABRISI:11:112#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:112#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:11:112#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says no verse was harder or more burdensome on the Prophet than this one; he told his companions that Hud and al-Waqiʿa had made him gray.
TABRISI:11:112#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ما نزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم آية كانت أشد عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r1.claim: Uprightness is continuing along one direction, unlike turning into divergent paths to the right or left.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r1.anchor: الاستقامة: الاستمرار في جهة واحدة، وذلك خلاف الأخذ في جهات اليمين والشمال،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r2.claim: The command is to persist in obeying the Lord's command and calling people to Him as the Quran directs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬4): معناه فاستقم على العمل بأمر ربك والدعاء إليه في {كما أمرت} في القرآن.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r3.claim: Although addressed to the Prophet, the command is intended for his community.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬5)، # والسدي (¬1): الخطاب له والمراد منه أمته.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r4.claim: The command is addressed to the Prophet but intended for his community.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬5)، # والسدي (¬1): الخطاب له والمراد منه أمته.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r5.claim: من تاب معك can be nominative by coordination with the subject of فاستقم, coordination with the subject of أمرت, or as a new sentence with an implied command to be upright.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ومن تاب معك} (من) في محل الرفع من وجوه؛ أحدها: أن تكون عطفا على الضمير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r6.claim: Those who repented with the Prophet are his companions who turned away from polytheism.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى {ومن تاب معك}، قال ابن عباس (¬2): يريد أصحابه الذين تابوا من الشرك.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r7.claim: طغيان means exceeding the proper limit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ولا تطغوا}، معنى الطغيان تجاوز المقدار،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r8.claim: Do not be arrogant toward anyone; be humble before God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3): يريد تواضعوا لله ولا تجبروا على أحد.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r9.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r9.claim: Do not exceed God's revealed limits by declaring lawful or unlawful what He did not command.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r9.anchor: وقال الكلبي (¬4): ولا تطغوا في القرآن فتحلوا أو تحرموا ما لم يأمركم به الله،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r10.claim: Another interpretation is simply not to go beyond God's command.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r11.claim: God sees human deeds, none of which are hidden from Him; He knew what people would do before they acted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p575#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا تخفى عليه أعمال بني آدم، علم قبل أن يعملوا ما هم عاملون.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r5.claim: The Prophet must persist in obeying his Lord and calling people to him, as the Qur'an commanded; his companions must also persist.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r5.anchor: يعني: أصحابه، أي: وليستقيموا هم أيضا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r6.claim: The companions should remain humble before God and avoid behaving arrogantly toward anyone.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r6.anchor: تواضعوا لله ولا تتجبروا على أحد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r7.claim: God sees all human actions, and none are hidden from him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:110-112/r7.anchor: لا تخفى عليه أعمال بني آدم

ELMALILI:11:112-113/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:112-113/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:112-113/r1.claim: Those who repented with the Prophet are all who repented from associating partners with God, joined him in faith, and became Muslims; they should be steadfast like him.
ELMALILI:11:112-113/r1.anchor: Seninle beraber tevbe edenler de yani şirkten tevbe edip de imanda sana iştirak ederek maiyyetinde bulunan, Müslüman olan her kimse de senin gibi müstakīm olsun

ELMALILI:11:112-113/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:112-113/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:112-113/r2.claim: Muslims must not exceed God’s bounds or deviate from the measure of steadfastness toward either excess or deficiency; God sees every deed and recompenses or punishes accordingly.
ELMALILI:11:112-113/r2.anchor: inhiraf edip de ifrat veya tefrîte sapmayın, aşırı gitmeyin ey Müslümanlar

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r14.claim: The positive commands are addressed grammatically to the Prophet but apply to everyone, while prohibitions address the community; this rhetorical shift implies that transgression and inclination to oppressors are inconceivable for the Prophet but possible among his community.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r14.anchor: zâhiren müfred olarak Resûlullah’a hitab edilmiş, hâlbuki mâna itibariyle emir, umûma yapılmıştır

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r15.claim: The subtle rhetoric here is what made the Prophet say that Sūrat Hūd made him old, because the community’s steadfastness faces danger.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r15.anchor: Peygamber’e شَي َّبَتْنِي سورة هُود dedirten de âyetin bu dakīk belâgatiyle ümmetin istikāmetinde öyle bir tehlikenin melhuz olmasıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:112/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:112/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:112/r1.claim: Istiqama in the Qur’an means comprehensive, continuous, consistent religious devotion and life; the verse combines uprightness as commanded with not exceeding God’s limits.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:112/r1.anchor: istikamet kavramı Kur’an’da “bütüncü, devamlı ve tutarlı dindarlık, dinî hayat” mânasını ifade etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:112/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:112/r2.speaker: Resûlullah
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:112/r2.claim: The Prophet said Hud and its sister surahs made him old, explaining that the command to remain upright as commanded was what aged him because it was especially difficult to fulfill.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:112/r2.anchor: Rivayete göre Resûlullah kendisine uygulanması bundan daha zor gelen bir âyet inmediğine işaret etmek üzere, “Hûd sûresi ve kardeşleri beni ihtiyarlattı” buyurmuştur

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r11.claim: Stand firm by fulfilling God's and creatures' rights: guard His rights, honor His commands, and guide creation, while seeing multiplicity in unity and unity in multiplicity without neglecting reverence.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r11.anchor: أي في القيام بحقوق الحق والخلق وذلك بالمحافظة على حقوقه تعالى والتعظيم لأمره والتسديد لخلقه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r12.claim: Those who repent with the Prophet are monotheists who leave selfhood and their sense of independent existence for the station of abiding after annihilation.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r12.anchor: ومن تاب ) عن إنيته وذهب وجوده ( معك من المؤمنين ) الموحدين إلى مقام البقاء بعد الفناء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r1.claim: One view says the Prophet's commanded steadfastness exceeds that of his companions; conjunction requires only sharing in the general act, not equal rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r1.anchor: إن الاستقامة المأمور بها صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فوق الاستقامة المأمور بها من معه عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r2.speaker: الجنيد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r2.claim: Junayd distinguishes steadfastness with fear and hope for worshipers, with awe and hope for the near ones, and without seeing one's own steadfastness for the gnostics.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r2.anchor: قال الجنيد قدس سره : الإستقامة مع الخوف والرجاء حال العابدين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r3.claim: Do not transgress means do not leave the limits set by sacred law; leaving them is heresy.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r3.anchor: ولا تطغوا ) ولا تخرجوا عما حد لكم من الشريعة فإن الخروج عنها زندقة

BURHAN:v3p303/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p303/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p303/r2.claim: The singular command lets direct address prevail over the absent persons joined to the Prophet; al-Zamakhshari instead supplies an implied plural command for them.
BURHAN:v3p303/r2.anchor: غلب فيه جانب أنت على جانب من فاسند إليه الفعل وكان تقديره فاستقيموا

BURHAN:v3p303/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p303/r3.speaker: الكشاف
BURHAN:v3p303/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses the command as if it said: remain steadfast as commanded, and let those who repented with you do so too.
BURHAN:v3p303/r3.anchor: قال صاحب الكشاف تقديره 2 فاستقم كما أمرت وليستقم كذلك من تاب معك

BURHAN:v2p410/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p410/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p410/r9.claim: The author rejects ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا as proof of a separator rule: a replacement for reinforcement must precede the conjunction, as in فاستقم كما أمرت ومن تاب معك.
BURHAN:v2p410/r9.anchor: وهذا لاحجة فيه لانها دخلت بعد واو العطف والذي يقوم مقام التاكيد انما ياتي قبل واو العطف

NASHR:v1p431/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p431/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p431/r1.claim: Hamza eases a quiescent hamza by replacing it with the homorganic long vowel of the preceding vowel: wāw after ḍamma, yāʾ after kasra, and alif after fatḥa.
NASHR:v1p431/r1.anchor: إن كان قبله ضم أبدل واوا، وإن كان قبله كسر أبدل ياء

NASHR:v1p431/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p431/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p431/r2.claim: The author rejects Maghrebi distinctions for hamzas at word beginnings: they are medial because they can be quiescent only when joined to what precedes, as in فاستقم.
NASHR:v1p431/r2.anchor: فلهذا حكم لهن بكونهن متوسطات. ألا ترى أن الهمزة في (فأووا، وأمر، وقال ايتوني) كالدال في (فادع) والسين في (فاستقم)

NASHR:v1p431/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p431/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو جعفر وورش
NASHR:v1p431/r3.claim: Abu Amr, Abu Jaʿfar, and Warsh ease all these cases without disagreement, treating them like other medial hamzas and replacing them.
NASHR:v1p431/r3.anchor: كأبي عمرو، وأبي جعفر، وورش فإنهم خففوا ذلك كله من غير خلف عن أحد منهم

NASHR:v1p431/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p431/r4.speaker: ابن الباذش
NASHR:v1p431/r4.claim: Ibn al-Badhish attributes full pronunciation of this group to Ibn Ghalbun, his father, and Ibn Sahl, but the author says al-Tadhkira explicitly has replacement without disagreement.
NASHR:v1p431/r4.anchor: والعجب أن ابن الباذش نسب تحقيق هذا القسم لأبي الحسن بن غلبون وأبيه وابن سهل

NASHR:v1p431/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p431/r5.speaker: أبو بكر بن مجاهد وأبو الطيب ابن غلبون وابنه أبو الحسن
NASHR:v1p431/r5.claim: One group breaks the hāʾ in anbihim and nabbiʾhum when easing hamza to yāʾ, by analogy with forms such as fīhim and yuʾtīhim.
NASHR:v1p431/r5.anchor: فهذا مذهب أبي بكر بن مجاهد، وأبي الطيب ابن غلبون، وابنه أبي الحسن

NASHR:v1p431/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p431/r6.speaker: الجمهور
NASHR:v1p431/r6.claim: Ibn Mihran, Makki, al-Mahdawi, Ibn Sufyan, and most readers retain the hāʾ's ḍamma because the following yāʾ is incidental; Ibn Ghalbun accepts both.

NASHR:v1p287/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p287/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p287/r5.claim: The contrast supports adjacency: Abu Amr assimilates ومن تاب من بعد ظلمه in al-Maʾida but clearly pronounces ومن تاب معك in Hud.
NASHR:v1p287/r5.anchor: والدليل على ذلك أنه مع إدغامه حرف المائدة أظهر ومن تاب معك في هود

NASHR:v1p287/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p287/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p287/r6.claim: The author lists ten following letters for taʾ assimilation and illustrates the list with بالبينات ثم.
NASHR:v1p287/r6.anchor: فالثاء نحو بالبينات ثم وجملته خمسة عشر حرفا

NASHR:v1p287/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p287/r7.speaker: ابن حبش
NASHR:v1p287/r7.claim: Ibn Habash transmits assimilation in الزكاة ثم and التوراة ثم through al-Duri and al-Susi; al-Dani read both routes this way.
NASHR:v1p287/r7.anchor: فروى إدغامهما للتقارب ابن حبش من طريق الدوري والسوسي

NASHR:v1p287/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p287/r8.speaker: ابن مجاهد
NASHR:v1p287/r8.claim: Ibn Mujahid prefers clear pronunciation in those two phrases because a fatḥa after a quiescent consonant is light; his students transmit it too.
NASHR:v1p287/r8.anchor: وروى أصحاب ابن مجاهد عنه الإظهار لخفة الفتحة بعد السكون

NASHR:v1p287/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p287/r9.speaker: ابن شنبوذ
NASHR:v1p287/r9.claim: Ibn Shanabudh uniquely assimilates the pronoun tāʾ in وإذا رأيت ثم رأيت, but the author rejects it as contrary to Abu Amr's principles and favors clear pronunciation.
NASHR:v1p287/r9.anchor: وانفرد ابن شنبوذ بإدغام وإذا رأيت ثم رأيت في الإنسان، وهو من تاء المضمر، وكذا روى أبو زيد
